newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia ministry confirms PGM export quota signed.
newsitem.headline: Russia ministry confirms PGM export quota signed.

text.p: The Russian government has signed a decree outlining platinum group metal (PGM) export quotas for 1997, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday, confirming reports last week that industry officials thought the decree was signed.
"Yes, the decree has definitely been signed," said Vladimir Rybkin, head of the precious metals department at the Finance Ministry.
But Rybkin said he did not know when long-delayed talks with Japanese buyers would begin.
"I can honestly say that I don't know about that. We have not received the full text (of the decree)," he said.
Officials at PGM export agents Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) were not immediately available for comment.
Last week Almaz deputy director Sergei Gorny told Reuters that he understood the quota decree had been signed, in which case talks with the Japanese could start soon.

A spokesman for the U.S. branch of Almaz later said that shipments from Russia, the world's biggest palladium exporter and second biggest platinum exporter, to Japan, the world's largest importer of both, should start late-May or early-June.
Platinum prices in London fixed at $395.25 an ounce on Monday, the highest fix since February 28. Palladium also climbed sharply, fixing at $171.75 an ounce, the highest level for over two years.
